Set up an AI model for mv_ask()

Source: R/ask-llm.R
mv_ask_setup.Rd

Chooses which AI model mv_ask() uses to understand plain-language requests and stores the API key so you only do this once. Three providers are supported through the ellmer package:

Usage

mv_ask_setup(
  provider = c("claude", "openai", "ollama", "none"),
  model = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  save = c("ask", "renviron", "keyring", "none"),
  test = TRUE
)

Arguments

provider

"claude", "openai", "ollama" or "none".

model

model name; defaults to "claude-opus-5-5" for Claude, the ellmer default for OpenAI and the first installed model for Ollama.

key

the API key. If NULL and none is set, you are asked for it with a masked prompt.

save

where to keep the key and settings for future sessions: "ask" (choose interactively), "renviron" (your .Renviron file), "keyring" (the system keychain, needs the keyring package) or "none" (this session only).

test

logical; send one tiny test request to check the setup.

Value

The provider and model, invisibly.

Details

  • "claude": Anthropic's Claude, with your own key from https://console.anthropic.com (stored as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

  • "openai": OpenAI's GPT models, with your own key from https://platform.openai.com (stored as OPENAI_API_KEY).

  • "ollama": a free model running on your own computer with Ollama (https://ollama.com). Install Ollama, run ollama pull qwen2.5 (or another model) once, and nothing ever leaves your machine.

Use provider = "none" to always use the built-in keyword parser, which needs no AI model and no internet connection.

Only a summary of your columns (see profile_data()) and your request are sent; never individual responses. Keys are never written into scripts, reports or mv_script objects.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mv_ask_setup("claude")
mv_ask_setup("ollama", model = "qwen2.5")
} # }
